title: Living in the Love of God | Sri Daya Mata
formattedMarkdown:
# Living in the Love of God

### Inspired by the Teachings of Paramahansa Yogananda
### Presented by Sri Daya Mata, Third President of Self-Realization Fellowship

To live in the love of God is to discover the ultimate sanctuary of the soul. In this deeply moving discourse, Sri Daya Mata, one of the foremost disciples of Paramahansa Yogananda, guides us into the inner chamber of our own hearts, where the Divine Mother waits in silence for Her children. She reminds us that the quest for human love, success, and security is ultimately a disguised longing for the one true Friend who will never fail us, never abandon us, and whose love knows no boundaries or conditions.

Throughout her decades of leadership as the spiritual head of Self-Realization Fellowship / Yogoda Satsanga Society of India, Sri Daya Mata exemplified this unconditional divine love. Her words serve as a warm, maternal beacon, showing us how to transform our daily lives from a series of mundane duties into a continuous, ecstatic conversation with the Divine.

---

### The Awakening of the Soul’s Yearning

Every human being is searching for a love that does not fade, a joy that does not lose its luster, and a peace that remains undisturbed by the storms of life. Sri Daya Mata teaches that we search for this fulfillment in the outer world, only to find disappointment. This disappointment is not a punishment; rather, it is a gentle nudge from the Divine, urging us to seek Him where He truly resides—within the temple of our own consciousness.

> "The soul cannot find permanent satisfaction in anything less than the Infinite. Every desire we experience is but a misdirected longing for God. When we turn our attention inward, we begin to realize that the love we have sought through countless lifetimes is already ours, flowing silently in the quiet depths of our own being."

To begin this journey, we must cultivate a sincere, burning desire for God. We must speak to Him with childlike simplicity and absolute sincerity. Gurudeva Paramahansa Yogananda often told his disciples that God does not mind our mistakes, but He cannot resist our love and sincerity. When we call to Him with a yearning heart, He must answer.

---

### Practicing the Presence of the Divine Mother

Living in the love of God is not an intellectual exercise; it is an active, daily practice. Sri Daya Mata emphasizes the ancient spiritual art of "practicing the presence of God." This means maintaining an unbroken, silent thread of communion with the Divine throughout all our waking hours, whether we are meditating, working in an office, preparing a meal, or serving others.

We can view God in whatever form appeals most deeply to our hearts. Sri Daya Mata found immense solace in approaching the Divine as the tender, forgiving, and infinitely compassionate Divine Mother. By viewing God as Mother, we lose our fear of judgement. We realize that just as an earthly mother does not abandon her child because of a mistake, so the Divine Mother is ever-ready to forgive, lift us up, and wrap us in Her loving embrace.

As we go about our duties, we can mentally whisper words of love to Her:

> "O Divine Mother, guide my thoughts. Act through my hands. Love through my heart. Let me see Thy face in everyone I meet today."

In this way, our work becomes worship, and the boundary between the sacred and the secular dissolves.

---

### The Altar of Silent Meditation

While practicing the presence of God throughout the day is essential, it must be supported by deep, daily meditation. Meditation is the cornerstone of the Self-Realization Fellowship path. It is the scientific method by which we quiet the restless mind and the turbulent senses, allowing us to perceive the subtle, inner vibration of the Spirit.

In the stillness of meditation, we withdraw our energy from the external world and focus it at the single point of the spiritual eye, the seat of intuition. It is here that we experience the actual, tangible presence of God as peace, love, light, and joy. Sri Daya Mata reminds us that we must not be impatient in our spiritual practice. The Divine Mother is not testing our perfection; She is observing our effort.

> "Do not worry if your mind wanders at first. Keep bringing it back to the thought of God. Every effort you make is a seed sown in the fertile soil of your consciousness, and in time, it will blossom into the beautiful flower of divine realization. Give your love to Him in the silence, and you will find His love pouring back into you a thousand-fold."

---

### Overcoming Obstacles with Dynamic Will

The path to divine realization is not without its challenges. There are times when the devotee experiences dry spells, when God seems distant, or when the habit of restlessness threatens to pull us away from our spiritual disciplines. During these moments, Sri Daya Mata counsels us to utilize our "dynamic will."

We must not be passive seekers. We must use our God-given willpower to overcome lethargy, doubt, and negative habits. If we do not feel devotion, we must pray for devotion. If we do not feel the presence of God, we must call out to Him with even greater intensity. Paramahansa Yogananda taught that dynamic will is the very force that bridges the gap between human limitation and divine omnipotence. When we align our human will with His divine will, we become invincible, capable of surmounting any obstacle that stands between our soul and its Creator.

---

### Spiritual Habits for Living in Divine Love

To help us anchor these profound truths into our daily routines, Sri Daya Mata suggests several practical habits that we can cultivate starting today:

*   **Begin and End Your Day in Communion:** Before your feet touch the floor in the morning, and just before you close your eyes in sleep, give your first and last thoughts to God. Thank Him for the gift of life and surrender your day into His keeping.
*   **Establish a Sacred Mantra:** Choose a simple phrase or prayer, such as *"I love Thee, Lord,"* or *"Thou art my life,"* and repeat it mentally during moments of transition—while driving, walking, or waiting in line.
*   **See the Divine in Others:** Practice seeing the Christ Consciousness dwelling within everyone you encounter. Look past their outer personalities, their flaws, or their differences, and salute the divine spark within their souls.
*   **Practice Selfless Service:** Seek opportunities to serve others without expecting anything in return. When we serve God in His children, we feel His love expanding within our own hearts.
*   **Incorporate Silence:** Set aside a few minutes of absolute silence each day, away from phones, screens, and distractions. In that quietude, listen for the still, small voice of the Divine.

---

### A Prayer for Divine Union

Let us close our eyes, quiet our minds, and unite our hearts in this prayer, holding the consciousness of Sri Daya Mata's maternal love and the sacred guidance of our Guru, Paramahansa Yogananda:

*O Cosmic Spirit, Divine Mother, Beloved Heavenly Father, Friend, and Guru!*
*Thou art the life of my life, the love of my heart, the light of my soul.*
*Forgive me for the times I have sought satisfaction in the transient things of this world, forgetting that Thou art the only true treasure.*
*Awaken within me an unquenchable thirst for Thy presence.*
*Let Thy love burn away all my limitations, all my fears, and all my doubts.*
*May my thoughts be ever centered on Thee, my hands ever busy in Thy service, and my heart ever beating in tune with Thy cosmic rhythm.*
*Reveal Thyself to me as the supreme Love that sustains the universe, and let me live forever in the sanctuary of that love.*

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma. Amen.*
